It looks okay but probably a bit high based on this angle. But yeh don’t think much valuable feedback from here 

Only comments would be you’re not bracing as well as you could be hence the slight movements on your way up / between reps. Drawing down the ribs with chest up is very useful cue for me before unracking and broadly just having a tighter setup across your back via a slightly narrower grip. 

Equally some small ankle collapse on the way down, my suspicion is from being 1-2 inches too wide with your foot placement but that’s just me guessing as you jump your feet out right before the first rep and at heavier weights combining this all together could lead to knee collapse, some ankle rotation, lack of core stability from bracing and leaving a lot of power output in the tank. 

My advice would be 1. Film a new angle 2. Work on your setup getting tighter across your back, through your core and play around slightly with foot placement (could be wrong on this one it’s just at a glance I think it doesn’t look super comfortable for you). Most of this is resolved before you even do a rep. 

Think you can probably move a lot more weight once you improve this, and if depth is an issue - would look into some ankle and hip mobility drills to do alongside your squat work 

All that said - it doesn’t look bad man these are all bits of advice I think may help you move more weight in a more controlled way - the strength is there imo
